name: Aardwolf Coordinates
author: Solao
description: Grid position from GMCP, with a target and the run command to reach it.
script:
--[[ aw-coords.lua Sean Stoves (Solao) — 2026-08-07 Where you are on Aardwolf's grid, and which way to walk. The big open zones put a coordinate on every room and tell you on arrival: Below the Basement Staircase {coords}0,30,20 'zone,x,y', or a bare '{coords}-1' where there is no grid. Vidblain is the reason this exists. It drops you somewhere random, the exits are at fixed coordinates, and nothing on screen tells you where you are — the tag is gagged, which is the whole problem. Set a target and this says how far and gives you the run command that walks it. Ported from the Mudlet module. Two things changed. It reads GMCP rather than the tag. room.info carries the position in a 'coord' object and always has, while the {coords} tag has to survive Core's gag and the 'tags' setting — and in Vidblain it never showed up at all, so the panel sat there saying 'No grid here' in the one zone this exists for. The tag trigger is still registered and still gags, it just isn't the source. See on_room. The axis learning is gone. Mudlet could watch what you sent through sysDataSendRequest and work out which way x and y grow; there is no such hook here. It doesn't need one: the answer was measured rather than assumed — 24,18 then 'run 2s5e' lands on 29,20 — so x grows EAST and y grows SOUTH. 'coord axes' flips either one if a zone ever disagrees. ]] plugin = { id = "aw-coords", name = "Aardwolf Coordinates", version = "1.1.3", author = "Solao", description = "Grid position from GMCP, with a target and the run command to reach it.", settings = { saveState = true }, } --[[ Drop every handler already on a widget event. Looked up through _G rather than called by name: a global this build does not have throws on the way IN, before pcall can catch anything, so a bare reference would take the plugin down on any client that lacks it. ]] local function drop_handlers(id, event) local ok, fn = pcall(function() return _G["unregisterWidgetEvent"] end) if ok and type(fn) == "function" then pcall(fn, id, event) end end -- @category widgets local TAG = "$Y[Coords v" .. plugin.version .. "]$w " local TAGR = "$R[Coords v" .. plugin.version .. "]$w " local VAR = "aw_coords" --[[ Aardwolf's own names for the ways out of Vidblain, straight off 'speedwalks'. These are the reason you'd set a target at all: every exit is at a fixed coordinate, and knowing you're 6 east and 3 north of Omen Tor is the difference between walking out and wandering. ]] local KNOWN = { ["omen tor"] = { 11, 8 }, ["asherodan"] = { 10, 15 }, ["darklight"] = { 14, 23 }, ["imperial"] = { 23, 4 }, ["sendhia"] = { 5, 6 }, ["fury"] = { 11, 26 }, } local cfg = { show = "always", -- always | coordareas | off target = nil, -- { name, x, y } xdir = "east", -- measured, not assumed; see the header ydir = "south", } local widget = nil local zone, cx, cy = nil, nil, nil local function trim(s) return (string.gsub(tostring(s or ""), "^%s*(.-)%s*$", "%1")) end local function esc(s) s = tostring(s or "") s = string.gsub(s, "&", "&") s = string.gsub(s, "<", "<") s = string.gsub(s, ">", ">") s = string.gsub(s, '"', """) return s end local function save_cfg() saveTable(VAR, cfg) end local function gmcp_get(names) for _, name in ipairs(names) do local d = getGMCPData(name) if type(d) == "table" then return d end end return nil end local function have() return type(cx) == "number" and type(cy) == "number" end local function in_vidblain() local r = gmcp_get({ "room.info", "Room.Info" }) return type(r) == "table" and string.lower(tostring(r.zone or "")) == "vidblain" end --- -- the way to the target --- local function opposite(d) if d == "east" then return "west" end if d == "west" then return "east" end if d == "north" then return "south" end return "north" end --[[ How far, and which way. Returns the legs as {count, direction} pairs so the caller can print them or turn them into a run — one place deciding which way is which, rather than two that can disagree. ]] local function legs() local t = cfg.target if not (t and have()) then return nil end local dx, dy = t.x - cx, t.y - cy if dx == 0 and dy == 0 then return {} end local out = {} -- north/south first: it is the axis people check against the compass if dy ~= 0 then local way = (dy > 0) and cfg.ydir or opposite(cfg.ydir) table.insert(out, { n = math.abs(dy), dir = way }) end if dx ~= 0 then local way = (dx > 0) and cfg.xdir or opposite(cfg.xdir) table.insert(out, { n = math.abs(dx), dir = way }) end return out end local function legs_text(l) if not l then return nil end if #l == 0 then return "here" end local out = {} for _, leg in ipairs(l) do table.insert(out, leg.n .. " " .. leg.dir) end return table.concat(out, ", ") end -- 'run 2s5e' — Aardwolf's speedwalk, count in front of the direction local function runcmd() local l = legs() if not l or #l == 0 then return nil end local out = "" for _, leg in ipairs(l) do out = out .. leg.n .. string.sub(leg.dir, 1, 1) end return "run " .. out end --- -- the panel --- local CSS = [[ ]] local function render() if not widget then return end local body = '
Location' .. '' .. '
hide
' .. '
' if not have() then body = body .. '
No grid here
' else body = body .. '
' .. '' .. cx .. ', ' .. cy .. '' .. 'zone ' .. tostring(zone or "?") .. '' .. '
' local t = cfg.target if t then local txt = legs_text(legs()) if txt == "here" then body = body .. '
' .. esc(t.name) .. ' — arrived
' else body = body .. '
' .. esc(t.name) .. ': ' .. esc(txt or "?") .. '
' local rc = runcmd() if rc then body = body .. '
' .. esc(rc) .. '
' end end end end setWidgetProperty(widget, "content", CSS .. '
' .. body .. '
') end --[[ Visible when it has something to say. 'coordareas' is the middle setting: only speak up where a grid exists, which in practice means the panel appears when you enter Vidblain or the Aylor street grid and gets out of the way everywhere else. ]] local function apply_visibility() if not widget then return end if cfg.show == "off" then hideWidget(widget) elseif cfg.show == "coordareas" and not have() then hideWidget(widget) else showWidget(widget) end end local function paint() render() apply_visibility() end --- -- where the numbers come from --- --[[ GMCP, not the tag. room.info carries them and always has: room.info { "num": 5922, "name": "...", "zone": "zoo", "coord": { "id": 0, "x": 37, "y": 19, "cont": 0 } } The {coords} tag reads the same but has to survive Core's tag gag and the 'tags' setting being on at all, and in Vidblain it simply never turned up — a panel saying 'No grid here' while the room plainly had a grid. GMCP is already flowing for the zone name, so this asks the packet that was going to arrive anyway. The tag trigger is still registered. It costs nothing, it keeps the tag off your screen if Core is disabled, and if it does fire it agrees with this. ]] local function on_room() local r = gmcp_get({ "room.info", "Room.Info" }) if type(r) ~= "table" then return end -- nested tables from the JS side need a type check before indexing local c = r.coord if type(c) ~= "table" then return end local x, y = tonumber(c.x), tonumber(c.y) local id = tonumber(c.id) --[[ A room off the grid answers -1 rather than leaving the field out, so 'is it a number' is not enough to call it a position. ]] if x and y and not (x < 0 and y < 0) then zone, cx, cy = id or zone, x, y else zone, cx, cy = nil, nil, nil end paint() end --- -- the tag --- local function cap(c, w, n) if type(w) == "table" and type(w[tostring(n)]) == "string" then return w[tostring(n)] end if type(c) == "table" then local base = (type(c[0]) == "string") and 0 or 1 local v = c[n - 1 + base] if type(v) == "string" then return v end end return "" end --[[ '{coords}zone,x,y', or '{coords}-1' for a room off the grid. Split by hand rather than with a pattern: this runs on a JS regex engine where the Lua classes mean nothing, and three numbers separated by commas is not worth the risk. ]] local function on_coords(c, line, w, raw) local body = trim(cap(c, w, 1)) local nums = {} local cur = "" for i = 1, string.len(body) do local ch = string.sub(body, i, i) if ch == "," then table.insert(nums, cur) cur = "" else cur = cur .. ch end end table.insert(nums, cur) local z, x, y = tonumber(nums[1]), tonumber(nums[2]), tonumber(nums[3]) if x and y then zone, cx, cy = z, x, y else -- '-1', or anything that isn't three numbers: no grid in this room zone, cx, cy = nil, nil, nil end paint() -- Core gags this too, at priority 90. Gagging here as well costs nothing -- and means the tag stays off the screen even if Core is disabled. return false end --- -- commands --- local function argv(args) if type(args) == "string" then local out, cur = {}, "" for i = 1, string.len(args) do local ch = string.sub(args, i, i) if ch == " " or ch == "\t" then if cur ~= "" then table.insert(out, cur); cur = "" end else cur = cur .. ch end end if cur ~= "" then table.insert(out, cur) end return out end local out = {} if type(args) ~= "table" then return out end local i = 0 while args[i] ~= nil do table.insert(out, tostring(args[i])) i = i + 1 end if #out == 0 then for _, v in ipairs(args) do table.insert(out, tostring(v)) end end return out end -- 'x,y' typed as one word or as three local function as_point(s) s = trim(s) local at = nil for i = 1, string.len(s) do if string.sub(s, i, i) == "," then at = i; break end end if not at then return nil end local x = tonumber(trim(string.sub(s, 1, at - 1))) local y = tonumber(trim(string.sub(s, at + 1))) if x and y then return { name = x .. "," .. y, x = x, y = y } end return nil end --[[ A name, exactly or unambiguously. Substring matching only answers when one name matches. pairs() order over KNOWN isn't defined, so a loose match used to resolve to whichever the hash visited first — and 'r' is in five of the six names. ]] local function as_place(s) local k = string.lower(trim(s)) if k == "" then return nil end if KNOWN[k] then return { name = k, x = KNOWN[k][1], y = KNOWN[k][2] } end local hits = {} for name in pairs(KNOWN) do if string.find(name, k, 1, true) then table.insert(hits, name) end end if #hits == 1 then local n = hits[1] return { name = n, x = KNOWN[n][1], y = KNOWN[n][2] } end --[[ ONE VALUE. NEVER TWO. This returned `nil, "a, b"` on the ambiguous path and one value on the other three, and the call site read it as `local hit, ambiguous = as_place(...)`. Multiple assignment transpiles to DESTRUCTURING, so the single-value paths hand a plain object to something expecting an iterable and the whole command dies with Plugin command error: TypeError: {} is not iterable A table either way, with the problem in a field. Nothing to destructure, nothing to get wrong at the call site. Same rule as cast_why in aw-spellup, and the same bug that took out aw-probe. ]] if #hits > 1 then table.sort(hits) return { ambig = table.concat(hits, ", ") } end return nil end local function send_run() local rc = runcmd() if not rc then utilprint(TAGR .. "no target, or you're standing on it.") return end --[[ Vidblain is a maze, so this walks the straight line and the MUD gives up when it hits a wall. Run it again from wherever you end up — it is a nudge in the right direction, not a pathfinder. ]] utilprint(TAG .. rc) send(rc) end local function status() utilprint(TAG .. "where you are on the grid, and how far to a target.") if have() then utilprint("$w here " .. cx .. "," .. cy .. " (zone " .. tostring(zone) .. ")") else utilprint("$w here $Kno coordinates in this room$w") end local t = cfg.target utilprint("$w target " .. (t and (t.name .. " " .. t.x .. "," .. t.y) or "none")) utilprint("$w to go " .. (legs_text(legs()) or "-")) utilprint("$w run " .. (runcmd() or "-")) utilprint("$w axes +x " .. cfg.xdir .. ", +y " .. cfg.ydir) utilprint("$w show " .. cfg.show) utilprint("") utilprint("$w Vidblain exits:") local names = {} for n in pairs(KNOWN) do table.insert(names, n) end table.sort(names) for _, n in ipairs(names) do utilprint("$w " .. n .. string.rep(" ", 12 - string.len(n)) .. KNOWN[n][1] .. "," .. KNOWN[n][2]) end utilprint("") utilprint("$w /coord set the target and show the way") utilprint("$w /coord run send the run for the straight line") utilprint("$w /coord clear drop the target") utilprint("$w /coord show off|coordareas|always") utilprint("$w /coord axes flip x|y if a zone disagrees about which way is which") utilprint("$w /coord raw what room.info actually says") end local function cmd(args) local a = argv(args) local verb = string.lower(a[1] or "") local rest = "" for i = 2, #a do rest = rest .. (rest == "" and "" or " ") .. a[i] end if verb == "" or verb == "status" then status() return end if verb == "run" or verb == "go" then send_run() return end if verb == "raw" then local r = gmcp_get({ "room.info", "Room.Info" }) if type(r) ~= "table" then utilprint(TAGR .. "no room.info yet.") return end utilprint(TAG .. "room " .. tostring(r.num) .. " zone " .. tostring(r.zone)) local c = r.coord if type(c) ~= "table" then utilprint("$w coord: $Rnot in this packet$w") else utilprint("$w coord: id=" .. tostring(c.id) .. " x=" .. tostring(c.x) .. " y=" .. tostring(c.y) .. " cont=" .. tostring(c.cont)) end utilprint("$w reading it as: " .. (have() and (cx .. "," .. cy) or "no grid")) return end if verb == "clear" then cfg.target = nil save_cfg() paint() utilprint(TAG .. "target cleared.") return end if verb == "show" then local want = string.lower(rest) if want == "off" or want == "always" or want == "coordareas" then cfg.show = want save_cfg() paint() utilprint(TAG .. "panel: " .. want .. ".") else utilprint(TAGR .. "/coord show off|coordareas|always") end return end if verb == "hide" then cfg.show = "off" save_cfg() apply_visibility() utilprint(TAG .. "hidden - '/coord show always' brings it back.") return end if verb == "axes" then local which = string.lower(trim(rest)) if string.find(which, "x", 1, true) then cfg.xdir = opposite(cfg.xdir) elseif string.find(which, "y", 1, true) then cfg.ydir = opposite(cfg.ydir) else utilprint(TAGR .. "/coord axes flip x (or y)") return end save_cfg() paint() utilprint(TAG .. "+x " .. cfg.xdir .. ", +y " .. cfg.ydir) return end -- everything else is a target: 'omen tor', 'fury', '11,8' local whole = verb .. (rest ~= "" and (" " .. rest) or "") local found = as_point(whole) if not found then local hit = as_place(whole) if type(hit) == "table" and hit.ambig then utilprint(TAGR .. "'" .. whole .. "' matches " .. hit.ambig .. " - be more specific.") return end found = hit end if not found then utilprint(TAGR .. "don't know '" .. whole .. "'. Try '/coord' for the list, or '/coord 11,8'.") return end cfg.target = found save_cfg() paint() utilprint(TAG .. "target " .. found.name .. " at " .. found.x .. "," .. found.y .. (have() and (" - " .. (legs_text(legs()) or "?")) or " (no coordinates here yet)")) local rc = runcmd() if rc then utilprint("$w " .. rc) end end function init() local saved = loadTable(VAR) if type(saved) == "table" then if saved.show == "off" or saved.show == "coordareas" or saved.show == "always" then cfg.show = saved.show end if saved.xdir == "east" or saved.xdir == "west" then cfg.xdir = saved.xdir end if saved.ydir == "north" or saved.ydir == "south" then cfg.ydir = saved.ydir end if type(saved.target) == "table" then local x, y = tonumber(saved.target.x), tonumber(saved.target.y) if x and y then cfg.target = { name = tostring(saved.target.name or (x .. "," .. y)), x = x, y = y } end end end widget = createWidget({ type = "html", name = "coords", title = "Location", position = { x = 16, y = 760 }, size = { width = 230, height = 132 }, visible = cfg.show ~= "off", appearance = { showTitleBar = false, autoHideSettingsCog = true, }, }) --[[ Clear first. init() runs again on every hot-reload and registerWidgetEvent APPENDS — so each reload stacks another handler on the same widget and one click fires all of them. It shows up as buttons sending their command two, three, five times, getting worse the longer a session goes on, and nothing about it looks like a plugin bug from the outside. unregisterWidgetEvent with no callback drops every handler for the event, which is exactly what a fresh init wants. ]] drop_handlers(widget, "action") registerWidgetEvent(widget, "action", function(data) if type(data) ~= "table" then return end local act = tostring(data.action or "") if act == "hide" then cfg.show = "off" save_cfg() apply_visibility() utilprint(TAG .. "hidden - '/coord show always' brings it back.") elseif act == "run" then send_run() end end) --[[ Above Core's tag gag, which sits at 90 and swallows the line. keepEvaluating so Core still gets it and the tag stays off screen. ]] addTrigger("^\\{coords\\}(.*)$", on_coords, { type = "regex", priority = 95, keepEvaluating = true }) onGMCPUpdate("room.info", on_room) onGMCPUpdate("Room.Info", on_room) registerCommand("coord", cmd, "Grid position, a target, and the run that gets you there") --[[ Core owns Core.Supports.Set and sends the union of what plugins declare. Room is here for room.info, which is the only way to know you are in Vidblain rather than some other gridded zone. ]] broadcastPlugin("aw-gmcp", "Room") paint() end
